approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and alternates one neural proposal batch with two graph-breeding batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population, with a real fresh neural parent protected at the first graph handoff. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior trained only on that objective's accepted scores samples functions over fresh offspring pools to choose the remaining graph evaluations. Accepted graph trajectories then train the neural policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and regularization toward the unchanged prior. The reusable prior still learns only the supplied molecular strings, even though the online neural sampler must compose new strings.
approach.novelty: Expose the unlabeled prior to two identity-equivalent traversals of a molecule: retain its original string and sometimes train on one checked atom-order alternative. This broadens the local sequence contexts in which the same molecular structure is learned without changing the molecule allocation or adding scored data. Neither sibling has changed prior serialization support; their difference was graph-offspring selection. The online learning, graph edits and posterior selector remain exactly as in the current Parent, so this experiment asks whether a less serialization-specific starting distribution supplies better material to the existing reciprocal search.

hypothesis: Train the reusable unlabeled recurrent prior on a half-original, half identity-checked alternative-SMILES serialization mixture for the same selected training rows, preserving the original holdout checkpoint rule and all online components.

finding_summary.headline: Alternative-traversal support and scores improve, while raw neural validity worsens
finding_summary.insights: This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.
finding_summary.results: The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and nitrogen-ring chemistry, with new selenium and unusual sulfur families, uneven size control and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories contain 4,500 evaluated molecules, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, across all three supplied replicas and all five tasks; the same 4,500 parent rows were read for comparison. The repertoire includes fused nitrogen heterocycles, phenols, carbonyl-containing rings, diarylamines, saturated amine rings, aryl alkynes and selenium heteroaromatics. All 4,350 emitted child SMILES parsed with the supplied RDKit environment, but graph validity is distinct from synthetic plausibility. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9839 to 0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.9609 to 0.9793; these are string-level presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Read-only RDKit measurements on optimizer rows give median heavy-atom counts of 26, 43, 29, 34 and 26 in the brief task order. Useful-looking medium-sized medicinal chemistry coexists with very small fragments, oversized linked assemblies, unusual heteroatom connectivity and strained-looking ring edits. Several seed-specific leading families differ substantially from the Parent, while many leading neighbors within each family remain close relatives. The structural-diversity judgment is therefore moderate despite numerous distinct molecular graphs. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit detects unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows respectively, and assigned tetrahedral centres in none. The observations describe output chemistry; they do not establish the cause of its change, a synthetic route, or measured stability.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest examples are medium-sized fused aryl/nitrogen systems: a phenyl-substituted indazole-like N-carbamoyl core fused to a gem-dimethyl oxygen ring, followed by phenolic diaryl pyrazoline-like compounds. The leading structure has 24 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 0 also explores aryl ureas and sulfur-linked carbamoyl groups attached to a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing an aldehyde. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with 624 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds; the Parent had medians of 25 heavy atoms and three rings and 529 such scaffolds. These counts include small ring edits and do not demonstrate an equivalent number of synthetically useful core families. The Parent high tail instead included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea arrangements. Thus the new output changes the core families while retaining extensive aromatic, donor/acceptor and carbonyl chemistry.
liabilities: Aldehyde-bearing four-membered unsaturated nitrogen rings and sulfur-linked variants need chemical scrutiny; their accepted graphs and scores do not establish accessible or stable compounds.

Both tiny heteroatom fragments and much larger flexible assemblies consume part of the observed proposal set. Sixty-five of the 870 optimizer rows contain a bond from N, O or S directly to a halogen, compared with 34 Parent rows under the same bond-based count.
Repeated phenol, heteroatom and ring-closure edits can change reactivity or geometry even when much of the favorable aromatic framework remains.
missing_features: Reliable exploration of compact alternative cores that preserves the useful aryl, nitrogen and carbonyl arrangement remains incomplete; many surrounding edits lose the favorable combination rather than cleanly substitute another core.
The pyrazoline-like saturated centres and other substituted ring junctions lack explicit stereochemical specification. No preferred configuration can be inferred from these observations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-carbamoyl leader scores 0.4811252243246881, its extra-phenol analogue 0.4588069837338257, and its ring-oxygen-deleted relative 0.458386638264238. Replacing the N-carbamoyl group by methyl in a late relative gives 0.387244764147529; extending one geminal methyl substituent to ethyl gives 0.34636729936804345. These local observations favor a particular compact ring/substituent arrangement, not indiscriminate heteroatom addition. A phenolic pyrazoline-like molecule scores 0.4201182934804424, while the aldehyde/aryl-urea family reaches 0.40910891241125485. In contrast, Cl, OO and OF each score 0.0, and a very large flexible polyamine/polyaryl molecule scores 1.8344487388079707e-40. The pooled median is 0.129972. Whole-molecule size and functional-group placement both matter in the observed gradient; these data do not identify a uniquely missing target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest high tail is concentrated in compact, mostly planar triazole-substituted aminopyridine pairs decorated with fluorine and chlorine. The leader has 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with a diarylamine bridge and several ring nitrogens. Its close relatives change small alkyl groups, halogen positions or fusion to the triazole. These look more conventional as synthetic targets than many of the large late seed-2 carbonyl/thione/sulfur-rich fused assemblies, although no routes are supplied. The full proposal distribution is much larger than its leading family: the child median is 43 heavy atoms and five rings, versus 36 and four in the Parent; 347 of 870 child proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, versus 128 in the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 85.5, maximum 197, and charged-marker rate 0.1724. Parent leading families included heteroaryl amino and acylhydrazone/imine connections; the new compact triazole/aminopyridine family changes their linkage chemistry without eliminating the large-assembly tail.
liabilities: The larger population contains extensive polyaromatic fusion, sulfur/carbonyl linkages, conjugated exocyclic unsaturation and multiple charges or ionizable groups. Their combined synthesis and physical-property balance are unestablished.
Halogen-rich heteroaromatic leaders are plausible motifs, but their observed scores do not demonstrate favorable solubility, stability or the utility of additional halogenation.
New short ring closures and fused arrangements can change geometry sharply. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 215 of the 870 child proposals, with no assigned centres.
missing_features: Compact alternatives that change the core or bridge while retaining the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are not well represented among the leading examples; most quoted leaders decorate the same aminopyridine/triazole family.

Controlled variation between compact and elaborated structures is uneven. The many large assemblies do not establish a missing objective-specific group, and their size is not required by the compact leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methyl-, ethyl- and differently halogenated triazole/aminopyridine examples all score 0.6220806794055203. A less halogenated close relative scores 0.6203208556149733, and an additional heteroaromatic ring gives 0.6203675187352428. The narrow spread suggests that local decoration changes do little once that ring/linker arrangement is present. A much larger late carbonyl-rich fused heterocycle still scores 0.6048855296308467, so large size is not uniformly rejected. Nevertheless, the bulky sulfone/amide/cyclic-amine low example scores 0.2889922015596881, and a very heavily brominated polyaromatic assembly scores 0.29217856536262243. The pooled median is 0.574287. These comparisons support useful heteroaromatic connectivity rather than a simple rule to maximize rings, halogens or size.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled high tail is an arylpiperazine/alkylamine family attached to chlorinated benzoselenophene-like rings. Many examples combine an aryl- or pyridyl-substituted piperazine with an additional tertiary amine and a flexible carbon linker. The leading example has 31 heavy atoms and four rings; a simpler high-scoring relative has 25 heavy atoms, a propyl linker and one arylpiperazine. Read-only atom counts find selenium in 174 of 870 child proposals, versus none of the 870 Parent proposals for this task. Other child seeds reach oxygen/carbonyl aromatic systems linked to saturated amines and sulfur/nitrogen heteroaromatics with substituted piperidines. The broader class of accessible saturated amines plus aromatic surfaces was already present in the Parent, whose leaders included diaryl aminoalkyl piperidines and linked saturated amine rings. The child median is 29 heavy atoms and four rings; the aromatic-marker rate is 0.9609. Its low charged-marker rate, 0.0149, does not mean basic centres are absent, because the molecules are written as neutral amines.
liabilities: The selenium heterocycle is unusual within the supplied Parent repertoire and adds an element-specific chemical liability that has not been assessed for stability or synthesis. It should not be called infeasible solely because it contains selenium.
Multiple basic centres, long flexible linkers and repeated aromatic units may complicate physical-property balance. The score alone does not establish those properties.
Some relatives add strained-looking short closures across aromatic frameworks, N–N connections or N–Cl bonds. The leading branched structures also leave tetrahedral configuration unspecified.
missing_features: No further required functional group can be inferred from a high tail already close to the score limit. Saturated basic centres, heteroaromatics and aromatic surfaces are represented.

Defined configurations and systematic linker geometry are not demonstrated for the branched amine family. The present data show missing stereochemical representation, without identifying a rewarded configuration.

Chemically matched conventional alternatives to the selenium-containing family are not established as a controlled comparison. Their absence prevents attributing the favorable whole-molecule score to the unusual element.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The extended pyridylpiperazine/tertiary-amine/selenium structure scores 0.9999994775753148, while the simpler propyl-linked arylpiperazine scores 0.9999993561334308. Removing the extra tertiary-amine branch still permits 0.9999980741980992 in a close family. Conversely, duplication into a much larger polyamine/selenium assembly gives only 0.03431111746034991, and the N-chlorinated nitrogen-ring example scores 0.00036530897832142426. The nitrofuran ester low example scores 6.212341904497256e-05 and an amide-rich heterocycle scores 7.81343751377966e-05. The visible association is with the whole aryl/saturated-amine/linker arrangement, rather than nitrogen count or maximal elaboration. Parent molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995, so the trajectory does not establish a selenium requirement or a chemically meaningful benefit from tiny differences near the upper score limit.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family combines an ethoxy-substituted fused conjugated carbonyl core with N-methylpiperazine, fluorine and an aryl or five-membered N–N/carbonyl appendage. Ring perception identifies a seven-membered conjugated carbonyl ring fused to a six-membered ring in the two strongest cited examples. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including an N-phenyl-substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl ring; a near-equal example has 34 heavy atoms, a bromophenyl group and a propionyl substituent instead. Other seeds explore densely fused carbonyl heterocycles and sulfonylated saturated nitrogen rings. These retain the Parent broad pattern of aromatic, carbonyl and saturated nitrogen-ring chemistry, but with different fused cores. The child median is 34 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and five for the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 63.8 and maximum 152. Common medicinal-chemistry substituents are present, while the complete leading frameworks remain elaborate and configurationally unresolved.
liabilities: Large fused conjugated carbonyl systems, multiple appended rings and rearranged short closures can make synthesis and geometry difficult to interpret; no route or conformational assessment is present.

The late high-scoring oxygen-fluorine analogue scores 0.21440741901011376 despite its unusual O–F bond. A favorable observation is therefore compatible with chemically concerning functional-group connectivity.
Duplication of substantial core fragments increases bulk without preserving the leading score in the cited late example. Several important saturated positions remain stereochemically unspecified.
missing_features: Less encumbered alternative cores that retain the favorable carbonyl/aryl/amine relationships have not been explored consistently in the leading neighborhood; near-equal simpler appendage choices show that additional ring complexity is not automatically helpful.

Configurationally specified variants of the substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl rings are missing. RDKit identifies two unassigned tetrahedral centres in the leading molecule and at least one unassigned centre in 511 of 870 child proposals.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-phenyl N–N/carbonyl appendage scores 0.22243686751733371 and the bromophenyl/propionyl alternative scores 0.22234616366476415. A benzyl-substituted N–N/carbonyl analogue scores 0.22082458431832067; the simpler bromophenyl/methyl relative scores 0.22050990442479085. These small differences do not establish that the extra saturated nitrogen ring or maximum carbonyl count is essential. The supplied Parent leading values include 0.2124137877466535 for a different fused carbonyl/amine architecture. A heavily duplicated late aromatic/carbonyl assembly scores 0.15308748742436262, while a one-carbon-linked close analogue retains 0.21606790785072147. Methane, OF and difluoromethanol each score 0.0, and a small acyclic fluorinated carbonate-containing molecule scores 0.018771276394456953. The observed preference is for connected aromatic, carbonyl and nitrogen environments; the data do not reveal a specific absent target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-1 family consists of fluorinated pyridyl–aryl alkynes bearing an oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group and an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre. In the leading SMILES that sulfur has an oxo bond, two nitrogen bonds, one carbon substituent and an explicit hydrogen; this is not the ordinary tetrahedral sulfonamide connectivity one might assume from a casual reading. The leader has 25 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. The [SH] text occurs in 160 of 870 child optimizer proposals, versus one Parent proposal for this task. Seed 2 instead reaches an N-methylated dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle linked through a fluorinated enone to a large conjugated nitrogen-containing ring; other output includes fused lactam/thiol chemistry. The Parent leading families included N-acyl triazolyl azetidines and hydrazino or nitroso-bearing nitrogen compounds. The output therefore changes its nitrogen/fluorine chemistry substantially, but the newer high sulfur family still lacks demonstrated ordinary chemical plausibility. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, versus 24 and three in the Parent.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing, highly coordinated sulfur environments and variants with additional N–S/O–N connections need explicit chemical review before being treated as practical molecules. RDKit parsing does not establish their stability or preparation.

Seventy-two of the 870 emitted structures have a direct N/O/S–halogen bond under a bond-based count, compared with 26 Parent structures. The cited O–F-containing high example shows that such connectivity is not confined to the low tail.

The alternative high family includes conjugated enones and large conjugated nitrogen rings; variants acquire N–F or additional ring fusion. These are possible reactivity and geometry concerns, with no supplied experimental assessment.
missing_features: Stable, ordinary-valence alternatives that preserve the useful local aryl/alkyne/nitrogen/fluorine arrangement are not established for the leading sulfur family. It would be incorrect to diagnose a general absence of nitrogen, fluorine or carbonyl chemistry.
Core changes that preserve that compact functional-group arrangement remain inconsistent; some late multiplication or relocation of otherwise familiar motifs leads to extremely low scores.

Stereochemically specified saturated and bridged alternatives are absent elsewhere in the output. These observations do not identify an objective-preferred configuration or prove that one particular missing heterocycle is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated aryl-alkyne structure with the unusual sulfur centre scores 0.5600222476080907. Its otherwise corresponding phenyl analogue without that aryl fluorine scores 0.5113964873062803, and shortening the sulfur-bound fluoroethyl group to fluoromethyl gives 0.4963704929462404 in the aryl-fluorinated family. A longer diyne relative scores 0.5252583563261087. Replacing the oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group by a direct O–F substituent still gives 0.4963704929462404, illustrating that this gradient does not certify normal reactivity. The separate dicarbonyl/enone family reaches 0.4853564671811107. In contrast, a large fluorinated polyaryl/alkyne assembly scores 0.0, a long polar guanidine/amide assembly scores 3.920867438776822e-82, and duplication of the late enone/heterocycle framework gives 2.250908533370224e-18. The pooled median is only 0.001751. Size, polar-group placement and exact connectivity are sharply consequential in these observations, but the high scores of atypical sulfur graphs do not reveal a missing conventional pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading aryl-alkyne molecule scores 0.5600222476080907 while carrying a hydrogen-bearing sulfur atom with oxo, carbon and two nitrogen bonds. Related O–F chemistry scores 0.4963704929462404, and a separate carbonyl/piperazine O–F analogue scores 0.21440741901011376. The full output also contains direct N/O/S–halogen bonds. Accepted molecular graphs and favorable scores therefore coexist with chemically questionable connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary functional-group valence and attachment chemistry when elaborating useful structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent functional-group replacements that retain useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships while distinguishing ordinary amines, amides, oxo-sulfur groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual heteroatom valence or heteroatom halogenation. Let accepted session feedback compare chemically coherent alternatives; do not treat valence parsing or score alone as evidence of stable chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set contains 347 of 870 molecules above 50 heavy atoms, compared with 128 for its Parent, while its leading cited structure has only 23 heavy atoms. Other low tails include methane, OO and OF at 0.0, and large duplicated amine or conjugated-carbonyl structures score 0.03431111746034991 and 2.250908533370224e-18. Some larger molecules still occupy high tails, so a universal small-molecule rule is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth and contraction do not reliably preserve an appropriate molecular scale or a coherent useful core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker alternatives that can vary size without removing the useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships or repeatedly joining whole successful molecules. Determine useful scale from the current accepted observations rather than imposing a task identity or treating size alone as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit inspection finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows in the supplied task order and no assigned centres. Cited pyrazoline-like rings, branched aminoalkyl groups and substituted N–N/carbonyl rings provide concrete examples; short closures and ring rearrangements also occur among high-scoring variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled ring geometry remain missing even when the output contains configurationally rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make specified configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction available while preserving useful surrounding connectivity. Separate changes in stereochemistry, saturation and ring geometry so their consequences can be learned from accepted feedback. The present absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper tails repeatedly decorate a fused N-carbamoyl core, an aminopyridine/triazole family, an arylpiperazine/selenium family, a fused carbonyl/piperazine family and an unusual sulfur-bearing aryl-alkyne family. Different seeds produce different families, and nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 624, 719, 632, 702 and 515 across the child sets. Many of those distinct graphs are local ring changes or elaborate assemblies; those counts alone do not establish useful core diversity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of useful, chemically distinct cores is uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall graph repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve access to more than one accepted core family and enable core replacements that retain spatial and electronic relationships among the locally useful groups. Compare core chemistry and functional-group arrangement rather than relying only on unique molecular identity, changed SMILES traversal or peripheral decoration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Selenium appears in 174 of 870 proposals in one child set and in none of its corresponding Parent set. The high child family has scores near the upper limit, but Parent amine/aromatic molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995. A shorter child linker architecture reaches 0.9999993561334308 near a more elaborate tertiary-amine example at 0.9999994775753148. These observations support an aryl/amine arrangement but do not identify selenium or extra complexity as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: New unusual-element families lack matched conventional chemical alternatives that would distinguish useful geometry from element-specific exploitation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep access to chemically matched element, ring and linker alternatives around accepted arrangements, including conventional heteroatom or carbon analogues when representable. Use actual session feedback to determine what the structure needs, without inferring element necessity from a single enriched high-scoring family or tiny near-limit score differences.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

activation_observables.measurement: Per supplied preparation seed, audit that the original sampled molecular-row schedule and original holdout split remain governed by the unchanged RNG stream and that replacement choices use a separate seed-derived stream. Report constructed alternatives, unique rows whose changed alternatives actually entered a gradient minibatch, number and fraction of such rows with adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original string, actual alternative versus original exposures, all fallback reasons and zero accepted identity/encode-decode mismatches. Independently reconstruct the bounded logged original/alternative pairs and their row-seeded permutation; compare against the Parent, whose source has zero alternative-row exposures and zero added same-molecule traversal contexts. The primary positive activation requires nonzero genuinely changed, identity-preserving alternative exposures and nonzero added contexts, not merely a larger vocabulary or cached candidates. Original and alternative holdout diagnostics additionally measure learned support; broader training syntax alone is not proof of useful scaffold coverage.

activation_observables.measurement: Report the unchanged original-string holdout row count and original token NLL before training and after selection for each supplied preparation seed, including selected checkpoint step and completed training steps. On the independently held-out, identity-checked paired alternatives report coverage, token NLL before and after training, and the original-versus-alternative gap at the selected checkpoint. A worse original or alternative likelihood is negative representation evidence, not grounds to rerun training or select another node.

approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and alternates one neural proposal batch with two graph-breeding batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population, with a real fresh neural parent protected at the first graph handoff. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior trained only on that objective's accepted scores samples functions over fresh offspring pools to choose the remaining graph evaluations. Accepted graph trajectories then train the neural policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and regularization toward the unchanged prior. The reusable prior still learns only the supplied molecular strings, even though the online neural sampler must compose new strings.
approach.novelty: Expose the unlabeled prior to two identity-equivalent traversals of a molecule: retain its original string and sometimes train on one checked atom-order alternative. This broadens the local sequence contexts in which the same molecular structure is learned without changing the molecule allocation or adding scored data. Neither sibling has changed prior serialization support; their difference was graph-offspring selection. The online learning, graph edits and posterior selector remain exactly as in the current Parent, so this experiment asks whether a less serialization-specific starting distribution supplies better material to the existing reciprocal search.

finding_summary.headline: Alternative-traversal support and scores improve, while raw neural validity worsens
finding_summary.insights: This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.
finding_summary.results: The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

finding_summary.headline: Alternative-traversal support and scores improve, while raw neural validity worsens
finding_summary.insights: This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.
finding_summary.results: The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

finding_summary.headline: Alternative-traversal support and scores improve, while raw neural validity worsens
finding_summary.insights: This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.
finding_summary.results: The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

molecular_assessment.headline: Rich aromatic and nitrogen-ring chemistry, with new selenium and unusual sulfur families, uneven size control and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The supplied trajectories contain 4,500 evaluated molecules, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, across all three supplied replicas and all five tasks; the same 4,500 parent rows were read for comparison. The repertoire includes fused nitrogen heterocycles, phenols, carbonyl-containing rings, diarylamines, saturated amine rings, aryl alkynes and selenium heteroaromatics. All 4,350 emitted child SMILES parsed with the supplied RDKit environment, but graph validity is distinct from synthetic plausibility. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9839 to 0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.9609 to 0.9793; these are string-level presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Read-only RDKit measurements on optimizer rows give median heavy-atom counts of 26, 43, 29, 34 and 26 in the brief task order. Useful-looking medium-sized medicinal chemistry coexists with very small fragments, oversized linked assemblies, unusual heteroatom connectivity and strained-looking ring edits. Several seed-specific leading families differ substantially from the Parent, while many leading neighbors within each family remain close relatives. The structural-diversity judgment is therefore moderate despite numerous distinct molecular graphs. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit detects unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows respectively, and assigned tetrahedral centres in none. The observations describe output chemistry; they do not establish the cause of its change, a synthetic route, or measured stability.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest examples are medium-sized fused aryl/nitrogen systems: a phenyl-substituted indazole-like N-carbamoyl core fused to a gem-dimethyl oxygen ring, followed by phenolic diaryl pyrazoline-like compounds. The leading structure has 24 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 0 also explores aryl ureas and sulfur-linked carbamoyl groups attached to a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing an aldehyde. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with 624 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds; the Parent had medians of 25 heavy atoms and three rings and 529 such scaffolds. These counts include small ring edits and do not demonstrate an equivalent number of synthetically useful core families. The Parent high tail instead included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea arrangements. Thus the new output changes the core families while retaining extensive aromatic, donor/acceptor and carbonyl chemistry.
liabilities: Aldehyde-bearing four-membered unsaturated nitrogen rings and sulfur-linked variants need chemical scrutiny; their accepted graphs and scores do not establish accessible or stable compounds.

Both tiny heteroatom fragments and much larger flexible assemblies consume part of the observed proposal set. Sixty-five of the 870 optimizer rows contain a bond from N, O or S directly to a halogen, compared with 34 Parent rows under the same bond-based count.
Repeated phenol, heteroatom and ring-closure edits can change reactivity or geometry even when much of the favorable aromatic framework remains.
missing_features: Reliable exploration of compact alternative cores that preserves the useful aryl, nitrogen and carbonyl arrangement remains incomplete; many surrounding edits lose the favorable combination rather than cleanly substitute another core.
The pyrazoline-like saturated centres and other substituted ring junctions lack explicit stereochemical specification. No preferred configuration can be inferred from these observations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-carbamoyl leader scores 0.4811252243246881, its extra-phenol analogue 0.4588069837338257, and its ring-oxygen-deleted relative 0.458386638264238. Replacing the N-carbamoyl group by methyl in a late relative gives 0.387244764147529; extending one geminal methyl substituent to ethyl gives 0.34636729936804345. These local observations favor a particular compact ring/substituent arrangement, not indiscriminate heteroatom addition. A phenolic pyrazoline-like molecule scores 0.4201182934804424, while the aldehyde/aryl-urea family reaches 0.40910891241125485. In contrast, Cl, OO and OF each score 0.0, and a very large flexible polyamine/polyaryl molecule scores 1.8344487388079707e-40. The pooled median is 0.129972. Whole-molecule size and functional-group placement both matter in the observed gradient; these data do not identify a uniquely missing target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest high tail is concentrated in compact, mostly planar triazole-substituted aminopyridine pairs decorated with fluorine and chlorine. The leader has 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with a diarylamine bridge and several ring nitrogens. Its close relatives change small alkyl groups, halogen positions or fusion to the triazole. These look more conventional as synthetic targets than many of the large late seed-2 carbonyl/thione/sulfur-rich fused assemblies, although no routes are supplied. The full proposal distribution is much larger than its leading family: the child median is 43 heavy atoms and five rings, versus 36 and four in the Parent; 347 of 870 child proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, versus 128 in the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 85.5, maximum 197, and charged-marker rate 0.1724. Parent leading families included heteroaryl amino and acylhydrazone/imine connections; the new compact triazole/aminopyridine family changes their linkage chemistry without eliminating the large-assembly tail.
liabilities: The larger population contains extensive polyaromatic fusion, sulfur/carbonyl linkages, conjugated exocyclic unsaturation and multiple charges or ionizable groups. Their combined synthesis and physical-property balance are unestablished.
Halogen-rich heteroaromatic leaders are plausible motifs, but their observed scores do not demonstrate favorable solubility, stability or the utility of additional halogenation.
New short ring closures and fused arrangements can change geometry sharply. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 215 of the 870 child proposals, with no assigned centres.
missing_features: Compact alternatives that change the core or bridge while retaining the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are not well represented among the leading examples; most quoted leaders decorate the same aminopyridine/triazole family.

Controlled variation between compact and elaborated structures is uneven. The many large assemblies do not establish a missing objective-specific group, and their size is not required by the compact leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methyl-, ethyl- and differently halogenated triazole/aminopyridine examples all score 0.6220806794055203. A less halogenated close relative scores 0.6203208556149733, and an additional heteroaromatic ring gives 0.6203675187352428. The narrow spread suggests that local decoration changes do little once that ring/linker arrangement is present. A much larger late carbonyl-rich fused heterocycle still scores 0.6048855296308467, so large size is not uniformly rejected. Nevertheless, the bulky sulfone/amide/cyclic-amine low example scores 0.2889922015596881, and a very heavily brominated polyaromatic assembly scores 0.29217856536262243. The pooled median is 0.574287. These comparisons support useful heteroaromatic connectivity rather than a simple rule to maximize rings, halogens or size.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled high tail is an arylpiperazine/alkylamine family attached to chlorinated benzoselenophene-like rings. Many examples combine an aryl- or pyridyl-substituted piperazine with an additional tertiary amine and a flexible carbon linker. The leading example has 31 heavy atoms and four rings; a simpler high-scoring relative has 25 heavy atoms, a propyl linker and one arylpiperazine. Read-only atom counts find selenium in 174 of 870 child proposals, versus none of the 870 Parent proposals for this task. Other child seeds reach oxygen/carbonyl aromatic systems linked to saturated amines and sulfur/nitrogen heteroaromatics with substituted piperidines. The broader class of accessible saturated amines plus aromatic surfaces was already present in the Parent, whose leaders included diaryl aminoalkyl piperidines and linked saturated amine rings. The child median is 29 heavy atoms and four rings; the aromatic-marker rate is 0.9609. Its low charged-marker rate, 0.0149, does not mean basic centres are absent, because the molecules are written as neutral amines.
liabilities: The selenium heterocycle is unusual within the supplied Parent repertoire and adds an element-specific chemical liability that has not been assessed for stability or synthesis. It should not be called infeasible solely because it contains selenium.
Multiple basic centres, long flexible linkers and repeated aromatic units may complicate physical-property balance. The score alone does not establish those properties.
Some relatives add strained-looking short closures across aromatic frameworks, N–N connections or N–Cl bonds. The leading branched structures also leave tetrahedral configuration unspecified.
missing_features: No further required functional group can be inferred from a high tail already close to the score limit. Saturated basic centres, heteroaromatics and aromatic surfaces are represented.

Defined configurations and systematic linker geometry are not demonstrated for the branched amine family. The present data show missing stereochemical representation, without identifying a rewarded configuration.

Chemically matched conventional alternatives to the selenium-containing family are not established as a controlled comparison. Their absence prevents attributing the favorable whole-molecule score to the unusual element.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The extended pyridylpiperazine/tertiary-amine/selenium structure scores 0.9999994775753148, while the simpler propyl-linked arylpiperazine scores 0.9999993561334308. Removing the extra tertiary-amine branch still permits 0.9999980741980992 in a close family. Conversely, duplication into a much larger polyamine/selenium assembly gives only 0.03431111746034991, and the N-chlorinated nitrogen-ring example scores 0.00036530897832142426. The nitrofuran ester low example scores 6.212341904497256e-05 and an amide-rich heterocycle scores 7.81343751377966e-05. The visible association is with the whole aryl/saturated-amine/linker arrangement, rather than nitrogen count or maximal elaboration. Parent molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995, so the trajectory does not establish a selenium requirement or a chemically meaningful benefit from tiny differences near the upper score limit.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family combines an ethoxy-substituted fused conjugated carbonyl core with N-methylpiperazine, fluorine and an aryl or five-membered N–N/carbonyl appendage. Ring perception identifies a seven-membered conjugated carbonyl ring fused to a six-membered ring in the two strongest cited examples. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including an N-phenyl-substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl ring; a near-equal example has 34 heavy atoms, a bromophenyl group and a propionyl substituent instead. Other seeds explore densely fused carbonyl heterocycles and sulfonylated saturated nitrogen rings. These retain the Parent broad pattern of aromatic, carbonyl and saturated nitrogen-ring chemistry, but with different fused cores. The child median is 34 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and five for the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 63.8 and maximum 152. Common medicinal-chemistry substituents are present, while the complete leading frameworks remain elaborate and configurationally unresolved.
liabilities: Large fused conjugated carbonyl systems, multiple appended rings and rearranged short closures can make synthesis and geometry difficult to interpret; no route or conformational assessment is present.

The late high-scoring oxygen-fluorine analogue scores 0.21440741901011376 despite its unusual O–F bond. A favorable observation is therefore compatible with chemically concerning functional-group connectivity.
Duplication of substantial core fragments increases bulk without preserving the leading score in the cited late example. Several important saturated positions remain stereochemically unspecified.
missing_features: Less encumbered alternative cores that retain the favorable carbonyl/aryl/amine relationships have not been explored consistently in the leading neighborhood; near-equal simpler appendage choices show that additional ring complexity is not automatically helpful.

Configurationally specified variants of the substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl rings are missing. RDKit identifies two unassigned tetrahedral centres in the leading molecule and at least one unassigned centre in 511 of 870 child proposals.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-phenyl N–N/carbonyl appendage scores 0.22243686751733371 and the bromophenyl/propionyl alternative scores 0.22234616366476415. A benzyl-substituted N–N/carbonyl analogue scores 0.22082458431832067; the simpler bromophenyl/methyl relative scores 0.22050990442479085. These small differences do not establish that the extra saturated nitrogen ring or maximum carbonyl count is essential. The supplied Parent leading values include 0.2124137877466535 for a different fused carbonyl/amine architecture. A heavily duplicated late aromatic/carbonyl assembly scores 0.15308748742436262, while a one-carbon-linked close analogue retains 0.21606790785072147. Methane, OF and difluoromethanol each score 0.0, and a small acyclic fluorinated carbonate-containing molecule scores 0.018771276394456953. The observed preference is for connected aromatic, carbonyl and nitrogen environments; the data do not reveal a specific absent target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-1 family consists of fluorinated pyridyl–aryl alkynes bearing an oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group and an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre. In the leading SMILES that sulfur has an oxo bond, two nitrogen bonds, one carbon substituent and an explicit hydrogen; this is not the ordinary tetrahedral sulfonamide connectivity one might assume from a casual reading. The leader has 25 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. The [SH] text occurs in 160 of 870 child optimizer proposals, versus one Parent proposal for this task. Seed 2 instead reaches an N-methylated dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle linked through a fluorinated enone to a large conjugated nitrogen-containing ring; other output includes fused lactam/thiol chemistry. The Parent leading families included N-acyl triazolyl azetidines and hydrazino or nitroso-bearing nitrogen compounds. The output therefore changes its nitrogen/fluorine chemistry substantially, but the newer high sulfur family still lacks demonstrated ordinary chemical plausibility. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, versus 24 and three in the Parent.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing, highly coordinated sulfur environments and variants with additional N–S/O–N connections need explicit chemical review before being treated as practical molecules. RDKit parsing does not establish their stability or preparation.

Seventy-two of the 870 emitted structures have a direct N/O/S–halogen bond under a bond-based count, compared with 26 Parent structures. The cited O–F-containing high example shows that such connectivity is not confined to the low tail.

The alternative high family includes conjugated enones and large conjugated nitrogen rings; variants acquire N–F or additional ring fusion. These are possible reactivity and geometry concerns, with no supplied experimental assessment.
missing_features: Stable, ordinary-valence alternatives that preserve the useful local aryl/alkyne/nitrogen/fluorine arrangement are not established for the leading sulfur family. It would be incorrect to diagnose a general absence of nitrogen, fluorine or carbonyl chemistry.
Core changes that preserve that compact functional-group arrangement remain inconsistent; some late multiplication or relocation of otherwise familiar motifs leads to extremely low scores.

Stereochemically specified saturated and bridged alternatives are absent elsewhere in the output. These observations do not identify an objective-preferred configuration or prove that one particular missing heterocycle is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated aryl-alkyne structure with the unusual sulfur centre scores 0.5600222476080907. Its otherwise corresponding phenyl analogue without that aryl fluorine scores 0.5113964873062803, and shortening the sulfur-bound fluoroethyl group to fluoromethyl gives 0.4963704929462404 in the aryl-fluorinated family. A longer diyne relative scores 0.5252583563261087. Replacing the oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group by a direct O–F substituent still gives 0.4963704929462404, illustrating that this gradient does not certify normal reactivity. The separate dicarbonyl/enone family reaches 0.4853564671811107. In contrast, a large fluorinated polyaryl/alkyne assembly scores 0.0, a long polar guanidine/amide assembly scores 3.920867438776822e-82, and duplication of the late enone/heterocycle framework gives 2.250908533370224e-18. The pooled median is only 0.001751. Size, polar-group placement and exact connectivity are sharply consequential in these observations, but the high scores of atypical sulfur graphs do not reveal a missing conventional pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading aryl-alkyne molecule scores 0.5600222476080907 while carrying a hydrogen-bearing sulfur atom with oxo, carbon and two nitrogen bonds. Related O–F chemistry scores 0.4963704929462404, and a separate carbonyl/piperazine O–F analogue scores 0.21440741901011376. The full output also contains direct N/O/S–halogen bonds. Accepted molecular graphs and favorable scores therefore coexist with chemically questionable connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary functional-group valence and attachment chemistry when elaborating useful structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent functional-group replacements that retain useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships while distinguishing ordinary amines, amides, oxo-sulfur groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual heteroatom valence or heteroatom halogenation. Let accepted session feedback compare chemically coherent alternatives; do not treat valence parsing or score alone as evidence of stable chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set contains 347 of 870 molecules above 50 heavy atoms, compared with 128 for its Parent, while its leading cited structure has only 23 heavy atoms. Other low tails include methane, OO and OF at 0.0, and large duplicated amine or conjugated-carbonyl structures score 0.03431111746034991 and 2.250908533370224e-18. Some larger molecules still occupy high tails, so a universal small-molecule rule is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth and contraction do not reliably preserve an appropriate molecular scale or a coherent useful core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker alternatives that can vary size without removing the useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships or repeatedly joining whole successful molecules. Determine useful scale from the current accepted observations rather than imposing a task identity or treating size alone as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit inspection finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows in the supplied task order and no assigned centres. Cited pyrazoline-like rings, branched aminoalkyl groups and substituted N–N/carbonyl rings provide concrete examples; short closures and ring rearrangements also occur among high-scoring variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled ring geometry remain missing even when the output contains configurationally rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make specified configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction available while preserving useful surrounding connectivity. Separate changes in stereochemistry, saturation and ring geometry so their consequences can be learned from accepted feedback. The present absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper tails repeatedly decorate a fused N-carbamoyl core, an aminopyridine/triazole family, an arylpiperazine/selenium family, a fused carbonyl/piperazine family and an unusual sulfur-bearing aryl-alkyne family. Different seeds produce different families, and nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 624, 719, 632, 702 and 515 across the child sets. Many of those distinct graphs are local ring changes or elaborate assemblies; those counts alone do not establish useful core diversity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of useful, chemically distinct cores is uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall graph repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve access to more than one accepted core family and enable core replacements that retain spatial and electronic relationships among the locally useful groups. Compare core chemistry and functional-group arrangement rather than relying only on unique molecular identity, changed SMILES traversal or peripheral decoration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Selenium appears in 174 of 870 proposals in one child set and in none of its corresponding Parent set. The high child family has scores near the upper limit, but Parent amine/aromatic molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995. A shorter child linker architecture reaches 0.9999993561334308 near a more elaborate tertiary-amine example at 0.9999994775753148. These observations support an aryl/amine arrangement but do not identify selenium or extra complexity as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: New unusual-element families lack matched conventional chemical alternatives that would distinguish useful geometry from element-specific exploitation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep access to chemically matched element, ring and linker alternatives around accepted arrangements, including conventional heteroatom or carbon analogues when representable. Use actual session feedback to determine what the structure needs, without inferring element necessity from a single enriched high-scoring family or tiny near-limit score differences.

Invalid and unterminated neural strings increase during the complete adapted-policy runs. High scores coexist with unusual sulfur connectivity, selenium-rich families, uncontrolled elaboration and missing stereochemical specification. Scalar feedback and RDKit acceptance do not by themselves establish stable, practical chemistry.

approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and alternates one neural proposal batch with two graph-breeding batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population, with a real fresh neural parent protected at the first graph handoff. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior trained only on that objective's accepted scores samples functions over fresh offspring pools to choose the remaining graph evaluations. Accepted graph trajectories then train the neural policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and regularization toward the unchanged prior. The reusable prior still learns only the supplied molecular strings, even though the online neural sampler must compose new strings.
approach.novelty: Expose the unlabeled prior to two identity-equivalent traversals of a molecule: retain its original string and sometimes train on one checked atom-order alternative. This broadens the local sequence contexts in which the same molecular structure is learned without changing the molecule allocation or adding scored data. Neither sibling has changed prior serialization support; their difference was graph-offspring selection. The online learning, graph edits and posterior selector remain exactly as in the current Parent, so this experiment asks whether a less serialization-specific starting distribution supplies better material to the existing reciprocal search.

research_intent.falsifier: The proposed preparation mechanism is refuted as implemented if no changed identity-equivalent alternative enters an actual training minibatch, if the consumed alternatives add no adjacent-token contexts beyond their own original strings, or if the alleged alternatives change molecular identity, erase stereochemistry, alter row allocation, leak heldout rows into training or modify an online Layer. A report of alternatives merely constructed but never trained is insufficient. Missing provenance that prevents identity and exposure audit makes activation inconclusive. The original holdout, frozen-prior and objective-isolation interfaces must remain intact. The scientific support hypothesis is weakened or refuted at its learned-representation level if a valid comparable audit shows no broader alternative-serialization likelihood support; increased exposure by itself cannot establish such generalization. More invalid or unterminated policy strings, weaker chemical coverage, or worse final scores after verified preparation activation are negative downstream evidence and must not be relabeled as nonexecution. Deadline-limited training must be reported because it can confound representational benefit with fewer updates; it must never trigger an unauthorized rerun.

research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-cc2d839e347b has a verified three-replica mean of 0.520669256395284 and standard deviation 0.00543180163495175. Its source trains the recurrent prior on only the one supplied serialization of each unlabeled corpus row; the source contains no identity-preserving alternative-SMILES training exposure. Its original-string holdout token NLL is already 0.562543, 0.565905 and 0.565284 across the three preparation seeds, but its actual policy trajectory logs contain 3524 invalid and 35 unterminated strings among 12000 raw draws across the fifteen objective sessions. They contain 1500 emitted, 6568 valid capacity-discarded and 373 duplicate draws, so emission fraction must not be confused with validity. Those draws come from the adapted policy, not an isolated frozen-prior assay. The supplied molecular assessment also finds uneven useful core coverage and unspecified stereochemistry despite varied rings and amines. Reciprocal handoffs and posterior selection already activate, so missing online execution is not the supported explanation. The specific limitation tested here is single-serialization learning of molecular syntax: low likelihood loss on that serialization need not confer support for the alternative traversal contexts that occur in de novo generation. This is a preparation-layer hypothesis, not proof that prior representation caused the chemical or score limitations.
